item.title: U.S. completes record Presidents Cup comeback
item.description: In a major reversal from Saturday's three-point deficit, the United States won nine of 12 Sunday singles and halved the last match to beat the International team 17-13. The biggest singles-day rout in Presidents Cup history extended the Americans' winning streak to 11.

item.title: Ravens beat Cowboys on seven-second drive in Rio
item.description: Baltimore needed only seven seconds to steal a 34-31 win in the NFL's first regular-season game in Rio. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers for 27 yards, the Ravens called timeout with one second left, and Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal.

item.title: Astros take AL West with an 81-81 record
item.description: Houston routed the Athletics 9-0 to win its fifth AL West title in six years despite finishing 81-81. The Astros became the first division champion in major-league history without a winning record, an odd final twist to baseball's expanded-playoff era.

item.title: Justin Verlander closes 21-year career with a family moment
item.description: Justin Verlander finished what he says will be his final major-league start, then watched 7-year-old daughter Genevieve sprint to the mound for a hug. The 43-year-old, a three-time Cy Young winner and 2017 World Series champion, walked off hand-in-hand with her after 21 seasons.

item.title: No. 21 Florida knocks off No. 4 Ole Miss, 52-28
item.description: Jadan Baugh powered Florida's 52-28 upset of fourth-ranked Ole Miss as the Gators turned a marquee SEC matchup into a statement win. Florida's ground game repeatedly broke through a defense that entered the weekend with national-title ambitions, reshaping the early conference race.

item.title: U.S. trims Presidents Cup deficit, trails by three entering singles
item.description: A day after the International side swept Friday foursomes, the U.S. answered on Saturday and cut the Presidents Cup margin to 10½-7½. That significant shift leaves the Americans within three points before Sunday's 12 singles matches at Medinah, keeping a comeback—and the International team's bid to end a long drought—alive.

item.title: Stephen Curry agrees to two-year, $116 million Warriors extension
item.description: Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension that would keep him with Golden State through 2028-29, his 20th NBA season. The Associated Press says the 38-year-old accepted less than the maximum available. If he stays, Curry could join Dirk Nowitzki, Kobe Bryant and Udonis Haslem as players spending at least 20 seasons with one franchise.

item.title: International team sweeps foursomes to take 7-3 Presidents Cup lead
item.description: A day after the U.S. opened with a 3-2 lead, the International team delivered a major reversal by sweeping all five Friday foursomes matches at Medinah. The Americans now trail 7-3, their worst two-session deficit since 1998—the only Presidents Cup won by the Internationals.

item.title: Macklin Celebrini becomes youngest captain in Sharks history
item.description: San Jose named 20-year-old Macklin Celebrini its 11th full-time captain, making him the youngest captain in franchise history and the NHL's youngest current captain. Joe Thornton presented the jersey. Celebrini fills a role left vacant after Logan Couture's career-ending injury.

item.title: Bob Pettit, two-time NBA MVP and Hawks champion, dies at 93
item.description: Bob Pettit, the first NBA player to win the league's MVP award, has died at 93. The Hall of Fame forward won a second MVP in 1959, made the All-Star team in each of his 11 seasons and powered the St. Louis Hawks past the Celtics for the 1958 championship — the franchise's only title.

item.title: White Sox complete historic turnaround with playoff berth
item.description: Chicago routed Kansas City 9-1 to clinch at least an AL wild card, becoming the first major-league club to reach the postseason immediately after two straight 100-loss seasons. The White Sox remain one game behind Cleveland in the AL Central with three games left against Colorado.

item.title: United States takes opening lead at Presidents Cup
item.description: Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns rallied to win the final fourballs match and give the U.S. a 3-2 first-day lead at Medinah. It was the ninth time in 10 Presidents Cups that the Americans won the opening session as they pursue an 11th consecutive victory in the biennial competition.

item.title: Darrell Waltrip diagnosed with brain disease, steps back
item.description: NASCAR great Darrell Waltrip, 79, has been diagnosed with frontotemporal degeneration, with possible chronic traumatic encephalopathy, his family said. The three-time Cup champion and 1989 Daytona 500 winner is stepping back from public life. His family said his symptoms remain minor and asked for privacy.

item.title: Padres move atop crowded NL wild-card race
item.description: Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as San Diego beat the Dodgers 5-1, moving the Padres into the top National League wild-card spot. San Diego has won 14 of 16 and reduced its postseason magic number to one, closing in on the franchise's first run of three straight playoff appearances.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo chases 1,000-goal milestone
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, begins another Portugal cycle under new coach Jorge Jesus with 979 career goals—833 for clubs and 146 for his country. Twenty-one more would make him the first player credited with 1,000 official goals. Ronaldo says reaching it would be the "icing on the cake" as Portugal also targets the Nations League.
